subject: Handoff: inference efficiency plan + kickoff for FluxAI
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Handoff: FluxAI - efficiency objectives + kickoff prep

Hi Laura,

Looping you in to hand off FluxAI (deal DEAL-8342). Quick context: they signed up for a Dedicated trial in eu-west and want a fast ramp — primary ask is to reduce per-token cost while keeping median tail latency under 220ms for short chat flows (~60–150 tokens). Key constraints: on-prem compliance for some workflows, but initial proof-of-concept will run in our eu hosted region.

What we captured in the MAP (attached):
- Target: 40–50% token cost reduction from baseline (current hosted config)
- Latency SLO: median <= 220ms, p95 <= 1s for 150-token requests
- Traffic profile: 65% short chat (<=80 tokens), 25% embeddings for semantic search, 10% batch batch scoring (larger seqs, 200–400 tokens)

Initial performance notes from bench:
- Baseline model: rw-13b (float16) on hosted pods; average cost 0.78x token unit; p50 ~250ms on our eu test shard
- Quick wins we think will move the needle: batching tuning for embeddings and scoring, prefix/KV caching for chat sessions, try quantized candidate rw-13b-int8 for scoring paths, and routing short-chat to a low-latency variant.

Suggested immediate tasks for kickoff (see Drive link):
1) Confirm the model variant set for canary (rw-13b / rw-13b-int8 / rw-7b-quant-int8)
2) Decide batch windows: target dynamic batching up to 8 for short chat, separate batching policy for larger scoring jobs (batch size 32 with async workers)
3) Enable prefix caching for returning session tokens and tune cache TTL
4) Routing policy: prefer dedicated eu pods for production; fallback to hosted with smaller batch sizes and model variant downgrade in outages

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx, fluxai_initial_perf_profiles.pdf

Soojin is our CS lead on tuning; Diego will lead the implementation. Can you pick a kickoff time this week? Marta was flexible around EMEA afternoon (CEST).

Thanks — I’ll be available for the call and to cover procurement/contract questions.

—Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

I’ll propose times separately. Diego, can you draft a technical checklist (infra, perms, observability hooks) we’ll want on the call?

—Laura

On Mon, Aug 15, 2027 at 11:04 AM Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> Soojin / Diego: I’ll take ownership of the engagement. Proposed agenda for kickoff (45m):

Adding the checklist below for the kickoff and immediate post-kickoff tasks. I'll bring this as a slide.

Kickoff technical checklist (short):
- Access: API keys for a staging org + sample traffic load generator (keys expiry 14d)
- Observability: token-level cost dashboard + per-route latency traces enabled (we need request_id header)
- Model variants: confirm rw-13b (float16), rw-13b-int8 (quantized candidate), rw-7b-quant-int8 (fallback)
- Batching policy: enable dynamic batching with target batch_time_ms=25ms, max_batch_size=8 for chat; separate worker pool for bulk scoring with max_batch_size=32, concurrency limiter
- Caching: enable prefix/KV cache for session tokens with default TTL=300s; plan for cache warmup strategy during canary
- Quantization guardrails: run synthetic regression on 200 reference prompts; quality tolerance p95 drop <= 2% on Rouge/BLEU-equivalent metric set
- Routing: prefer "eu-dedicated" pool for production; route to hosted fallback with explicit model downgrade and reduced batch size on capacity signal
- Rollout: Canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback on cost or quality regressions; map thresholds in the MAP doc
- Deliverables week 1: perf report, canary config, and rollback playbook

I’ll also prepare a short checklist for infra team: network egress allowances, KMS access notes, and sample workload generator steps.

—Diego
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
